findings.reason: the plan must name the alternative transformer and say why the envelope (an imas-ink helper) is the owner rather than a data transformer, or adopt the transformer; an unsearched altair mechanism is the plan's own reuse_search gap, and its premise ("cannot be drawn at all") is falsified by `disable_max_rows()`.
findings.text: §1 adds a bespoke min/max envelope to `_render_timeseries_alt` on the premise that "a long series cannot be drawn in altair at all today", but altair ships two data-transformer mechanisms for exactly this, neither cited or rejected: `alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()` (which lets a 300,000-row series render — the same series that raises `MaxRowsError` at 5,000 rows, reproduced) and the `vegafusion` transformer named verbatim in that error message and registered in the installed altair (`alt.data_transformers.names()` → `['csv','default','json','vegafusion']`; package absent here).

reuse_search-1.reason: alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows() lets the chart render by embedding every one of the 300,000 samples in the chart spec, which is the file-size problem this plan exists to fix; the vegafusion transformer adds a dependency and a server-side compute step for what a 4,000-point min/max envelope does locally, so the envelope stays

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1's envelope hides binning plus time-ordered min/max selection behind one private function in `imas_ink/_decimate.py`, and §2 hides label suppression behind the existing private renderer keyword rather than spreading wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the two new constants land in `imas_ink/style.py` (`InkStyle`), the module the project declares as the single source of visual constants, and the altair-side helper has no existing owner in imas-ink to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 adds two `InkStyle` constants and states in its own text that nothing bounds a figure's path resolution today so they retire nothing, and §2 adds no public name.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan reuses matplotlib's own `path.simplify_threshold` and extends the existing `label_axes` mechanism, but proposes a bespoke min/max envelope in `imas_ink/_decimate.py` without citing altair's own row-limit machinery (`alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()` / the `vegafusion` transformer), which its own `MaxRowsError` names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 extends the existing `label_axes` suppression path (and calls the private renderers directly, as `time_trace_figure_mpl` already does) rather than clearing labels after drawing; §1 routes the matplotlib bound through matplotlib's own simplifier instead of wrapping it.
